CITY OF ALHAMBRA PLANNING COMMISSION
  ACTION MINUTES

  Regular Meeting
  June 6, 2022

A.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER:  7:00 P.M. via video conference and teleconference

B.  ROLL CALL:
  Present:  Ho, Juarez, Mojarro, Olson, Pham, Sahu, Tsujii, Wang, Garcia, Gardea

  Absent:  None

  Staff Present: Vanessa Reynoso, Deputy Director, Paul Lam, Principal Planner, Alondra
  Espinosa, Deputy City Attorney

C.  FLAG SALUTE:  Led by President Gardea

D.  CONSENT AGENDA:

  ITEM 1:  MINUTES – MAY 16, 2022
  • Request: This is a request for the Planning Commission to approve
  the Minutes of the May 16, 2022, Regular Meeting of the Alhambra
  Planning Commission.
  • Recommended Action: Commission review and approve as
  submitted the Minutes of the May 16, 2022, Regular Meeting of the
  Alhambra Planning Commission.

  ITEM 2:  EXTENSION FOR PLANNED DEVELOPMENT PERMIT PD-20-34
  • 749-801 South Sierra Vista Avenue
  • Request: This is a request for a one-year time extension for the
  previously approved Planned Development Permit PD-20-34 to
  develop an 18-unit condominium complex on an approximate land
  area of 27,020 square feet located in the R-3 (Multiple Family
  Residential) zone.
  • Recommended Action: Adopt Resolution 22-18 approving a one-
  year time extension for Planned Development Permit PD-20-34,
  subject to the Conditions of Approval.

  ITEM 3:  FINDING OF PUBLIC CONVENIENCE OR NECESSITY
  • 300 West Main Street, Unit 120
  • Request: This is a request for Finding of Public Convenience or
  Necessity (PCN) in association with an approved Conditional Use
  Permit for Good Fortune Market, located in the Alhambra Pacific
  Plaza Specific Plan zone.
  1
  6/06/2022
   •  Recommended Action: Adopt Resolution 22-19 approving a
  Finding of Public Convenience or Necessity for alcohol sales at 300
  West Main Street, Unit 120.

  MOTION:
  •  Moved to approve Consent Agenda Items 1, 2 and 3.
  •  Moved by Vice President Garcia, Seconded by Commissioner Olson.
  •  The motion carried by the following roll call vote:

  Item 1
  Roll Call Vote: 8-0-2
  Ayes:  Ho, Juarez, Mojarro, Olson, Tsujii, Wang, Garcia, Gardea
  Noes:  None
  Abstain: Pham, Sahu
  Absent: None

  Item 2 and 3
  Roll Call Vote: 10-0
  Ayes:  Ho, Juarez, Mojarro, Olson, Pham, Sahu, Tsujii, Wang,
  Garcia, Gardea
  Noes:  None
  Abstain: None
  Absent: None

  •  For additional information regarding the discussion, the audio and video
  recordings of the discussion is available here:
  Audio:
  https://www.cityofalhambra.org/DocumentCenter/View/3397/PC-Meeting-6-6-2022-
  Audio-Recording-MP3
  Video:
  https://www.cityofalhambra.org/DocumentCenter/View/3396/PC-Meeting-6-6-2022-
  video-MP4

E.  DISCUSSION ITEMS:

  •  There were no Discussion items.

F:  PUBLIC HEARINGS:

  ITEM 4:  PLANNED DEVELOPMENT PERMITS PD-21-26 & PD-22-09 AND
  VARIANCES VAR-21-08 & VAR-22-04
  • 230-234 West Main Street and 236 West Main Street
  • Request: This is an application for two Planned Development
  Permits and two Variances for adjacent buildings on separate lots
  located at 230-234 West Main Street and 236 West Main Street. The
  request is to allow a food service establishment (a coffee shop) that
  2
  6/06/2022
   would span the first floor frontage of both lots into a combined
  furniture retail showroom/coffee shop at 230-234 W. Main St. only.
  Co-working office use is proposed for the areas behind the food
  service use at 236 W. Main St., as well as the area behind the furniture
  retail showroom/coffee shop and the second floor at 230-234 W. Main
  St. The Variances requested are to seek relief from the required
  number of parking spaces for both addresses. The subject properties
  are located in the Central Business District-Downtown Revitalization
  District (CBD-DRD) zone in the City of Alhambra.
  •  Recommended Action: Adopt Resolution 22-16 approving Planned
  Development Permit PD-21-26 and Variance VAR-21-08, subject to
  the Conditions of Approval; and adopt Resolution 22-17 approving
  Planned Development Permit PD-22-09 and Variance VAR-22-04,
  subject to the Conditions of Approval.
  •  Principal Planner Paul Lam provided Staff presentation.
  •  Jerome Chang, applicant, was available to answer questions.
  •  Commissioner Comments:
  Commissioner Sahu noted an error in the RECOMMENDATION
  being displayed on the screen. Also, Commissioner Sahu verified the
  previous entitlement approval for this location was similar in nature
  but required more parking spaces.
  Commissioner Wang clarified that the Planned Development Permit
  applications were required because the buildings were both vacant for
  longer than six (6) months. She also inquired if the City documents
  the reasons for why businesses close.
  President Gardea clarified under what circumstances a Planned
  Development Permit application is required. He also inquired if Staff
  was aware of how long the last business occupied the space and if the
  City tracked the overall number of Variances granted to the
  Downtown businesses. Commissioner Wang stated that tracking the
  number of Variances would be of value.
  Commissioner Wang alerted Staff that Commissioner Mojarro had
  dropped connection and needed to be readmitted into the Panel.
  Commissioner Mojarro was readmitted into the Panel.
  •  Public Comments:
  There were none.

MOTION:
  •  Moved to approve Planned Development Permit PD-21-26 and Variance
  VAR-21-08, and Planned Development Permit PD-22-09 and Variance
  VAR-22-04.
  •  Moved by Commissioner Sahu, Seconded by Commissioner Wang.
  •  The motion carried by the following roll call vote:

  Roll Call Vote: 10-0
  Ayes:  Ho, Juarez, Mojarro, Olson, Pham, Sahu, Tsujii, Wang,
  Garcia, Gardea
  3
  6/06/2022
   Noes:  None
  Abstain:  None
  Absent:  None

G.  DIRECTOR’S REPORT:

  •  There were no Director’s Report items.

H.  PUBLIC COMMENTS/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS:

  •  There were no public comments.

I.  COMMISSION ORALS:

  •  Commissioner Pham stated that it would be helpful for the Planning Commission to
  know the utilization rates of the public parking facilities. Commissioner Sahu recalled
  that the Commission had been provided such information previously.
  •  Commissioner Sahu noted the high volume of traffic and the lack of parking spaces
  in front of the main Post Office and inquired if the City could look into the matter.
  •  President Gardea informed the Commission that he may not be available for the next
  regularly scheduled meeting of the Planning Commission.
  •  Commissioner Wang reiterated the importance of having data showing how the public
  parking facilities are being used. She asked for a brief update on the Zoning Code
  Update project. She also commended Staff for their job performance while being
  understaffed.
